This leads to the concept of retinal dimensionality, where each point in the visual field corresponds to a unique spatial extent. The second operator, depth realization, bridges the gap between retinal input and perceived distance by integrating locomotor context. This dual modality ensures spontaneous and robust depth perception. The third operator, homogeneous space, asserts that these dimensions are not only measurable but also uniformly experienced, enabling commensurability. These operators form a triadic structure: one grounded in sensory input, one in behavioral integration, and one in perceptual consistency. Failure modes arise when these modalities decouple—such as in visual illusions or neurological deficits—where the retinal map becomes misaligned with locomotor experience, or when spatial dimensions lose their uniformity.
